title: Rescue path for partial-session rewrites and ledger drift during opaque proxying
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background:

We observed cases where client traffic goes through an opaque HTTP/WSS proxy that performs on-the-fly rewrites (attachments stripping, header injection, content-mangling for A/B proxies). Those rewrites sometimes change token counts or chunk boundaries without the client or upstream server coordinating. The metering pipeline (prefix attribution + session ledger) expects stable boundaries; mid-session opaque rewrites lead to small but measurable ledger drift (provisional credits not reconciled, duplicated attribution, or orphaned debits).

Observed symptoms:
- Small daily billing discrepancies for tenants behind certain proxies (~0.05% of volume)
- Resolved by manual backfill in one customer case; root cause traced to partial rewrite + reconnect path where the proxy re-encoded a multipart payload and changed UTF-8 split points.

Goal:
Implement a deterministic "rescue path" in the metering pipeline that detects and reconciles ledger drift caused by partial-session rewrites from opaque proxies, while preserving SLOs and avoiding recharging customers for legitimate retry/resume semantics. The fix must be auditable and reversible, and expose telemetry to prove correctness to customers and Finance.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Pipeline emits a reconciliation event when session-level token delta exceeds threshold (configurable).
2) Reconciliation produces an immutable audit record showing pre- and post-fix ledger entries and justification.
3) No customer receives duplicate charges in >99.99% of simulated proxy-rewrite replays.
4) Unit and e2e harnesses reproduce previously observed drift case and validate ledger alignment.
5) Feature guarded behind a runtime flag and enabled gradually with monitoring alerts.
technical_approach:
Summary:
- Detect: add a lightweight session-scanner that computes a rolling checksum and token-length histogram at key checkpoints (ingest, pre-encode, post-encode).
- Heuristics: when checkpoints disagree beyond configurable tolerance we classify session as 'drift-suspect' and enqueue for reconciliation.
- Rescue path: compute minimal delta by aligning last stable checkpoint to current stream using fuzzy boundary heuristics (byte/UTF-8 aware, tokenization-aware). Create a provisional correction transaction (debit/credit) that is idempotent and queryable.
- Audit: write reconciliation records to immutable ledger (append-only) with links to request IDs, proxy headers, and checksum artifacts.
- Safety: limit automatic corrections to low-cost thresholds; otherwise escalate to manual review workflow.
- Performance: keep checkpointing inexpensive (sampling + compact hash), avoid per-token ops in fast path.

Implementation notes:
- Reuse existing checksum format from ENG-314159 to keep compatibility.
- Add a reconciliation queue consumer with rate limit and backoff so it cannot overload the accounting DB.
- Provide a dry-run mode that emits corrections to the audit stream but does not apply credits/debits.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for checksum and fuzzy aligner across concatenation, split-utf8, and stuffing cases.
2) End-to-end replay harness that replays recorded proxy re-encodings from the incident reproducer (see attachments).
3) Fuzz test: generate random rewrite transforms (strip attachments, header injection, chunk rewrap) and assert ledger delta either 0 or within tolerated correction window.
4) Staging canary: dark launch corrections against a shadow billing ledger and compare with production ledger for divergence.
5) QA checklist: verify audit records contain minimal PII and have stable links to trace-id and archived payload sample.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 0 (week 1): Implement detectors + dark-run rescue that writes audit-only records. Enable for 1% traffic.
- Phase 1 (week 2): Enable dry-run corrections (no monetary changes) for 20% traffic, build dashboards and alerts.
- Phase 2 (week 3): Allow low-cost automated corrections (threshold <= $0.50 equivalent) for 50% traffic.
- Phase 3 (week 4): Full enable with guardrails; manual review path for corrections exceeding threshold.
- Abort: roll back runtime flag if reconciliation error rate > 0.1% or if latency regresses beyond 5th percentile SLO.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Metrics to add:
- meter.rescue.detected.count (tags: service, region, proxy-fingerprint)
- meter.rescue.corrections.applied.count
- meter.rescue.dryrun.count
- meter.rescue.latency.p95
- meter.rescue.audit.size_bytes.p95
Alerts:
- >100 detected sessions in 10m without a single dry-run correction -> investigate false positives
- >1% correction failure rate over 1h -> rollback flag
Dashboards:
- Per-tenant drift heatmap, reconciliation success rate, audit-event samples.
Logging:
- Include compact checksum, trace-id, session-id, and probe reason. Avoid storing full user content in logs.
risks_and_mitigations:
1) Risk: Overcorrecting and double-charging customers. Mitigation: default to dry-run, policy caps, and manual review thresholds.
2) Risk: Performance overhead on hot path. Mitigation: sample-based checkpoints and async reconciliation consumers.
3) Risk: Audit storage blowup. Mitigation: store compressed checkpoints and rotate per retention policy.
4) Risk: Edge rewrites that alter semantics (e.g., canonicalization differences). Mitigation: coordinate with proxy teams to publish fingerprinting headers; add opt-out via tenant config.
